sources.title: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus: Western Wei
sources.note: Institutional chronology and art summary, directly read. Its 535 to 556 stylistic range precedes its stated Northern Zhou inauguration in 557; use indexed political interval 535 to 557. Do not reproduce erroneous Yuwen Tai reign dates or Spanish BCE typo.

sources.title: Albert E. Dien, Western Wei to Northern Zhou, Cambridge History of China (2019), chapter 10
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly available; supports western successor state and Yuwen family military-colony background. No claims depend on paywalled chapter text.

sources.title: Yoshitaka Maejima, Regarding the bureaucratic structure of the regime of Yuwen Tai of the Western Wei (2011)
sources.note: Complete English scholarly abstract verified in indexed CiNii original. Direct page challenges automated access. Distinguishes staff organization from territorial government, 553 reorganization and 556 Zhouli-based system.

sources.title: Book of Zhou, chapter 23: biography of Su Chuo, primary text
sources.note: Directly read transmitted Chinese text. Policy statements are prescriptions recorded in a later dynastic history, not measured outcomes. Agricultural and textile passages distinguish obligations and household labor; final paragraph specifies official learning requirements. Count the entire Book of Zhou as one underlying work for reuse review.

sources.title: Liu Wei-chi, Cultural Elements of Western Wei and Northern Zhou Tomb Guardians: Workshops and Styles, National Palace Museum Research Quarterly 41.2
sources.note: Official indexed PDF read: title page, p. 4 workshop discussion and appendix rows Lu Chou 538 and Princess Huihua 541. Public PDF subsequently downloaded and appendix p. 42 visually checked in npm-page42-large.png; confirms toilets and grain pounders despite erroneous search OCR. Search exact URL with tomb year and 厠, or title; alternate official internationalized domain exposes same PDF. These are miniature funerary furnishings, not excavated functional toilets. Lu name is 陸醜, occasionally OCR corrupted as 陸瓢.

sources.title: Dunhuang Academy: Mogao Cave 285
sources.note: Direct institutional description, dated inscriptions 538/539, layout, musicians, Chinese and Indian deities and later repainting. Avoid treating debated meditation function as certain, or mythological narratives as ordinary street scenes.

sources.title: Zhang Yuanlin, Interpretation of Mogao Cave 285 from the Perspective of the Lotus Sutra, translated by Neil Schmid
sources.note: Direct scholarly PDF, printed p. 19 (PDF page 11) gives the fourth-year inscription and translation; pp. 20 and 24 discuss local donors, with elite identification explicitly an interpretation. Printed pp. 27 to 28 identify Shiva, Kumara and Ganesha.

sources.title: Guo Qinglin and colleagues, Radiocarbon Chronology for Early Caves of the Mogao Grottoes at Dunhuang, China (2010)
sources.note: Direct study, Radiocarbon 52, pp. 500 to 510. Abstract and materials section p. 502 describe plant fibers in plaster, statue cores, samples and consistency of cave 285 results with inscriptions.

sources.title: Kwon Youngwoo, The Multipurpose Meditation Cave: Rethinking the Function of Mogao Cave 285 in Dunhuang (2015)
sources.note: Primary scholar abstract read in official Korean Citation Index; interpretation connects meditation with ordination and repentance. Supports uncertainty about function, not a proven timetable of practice.

sources.title: Ye Xiong, A Newly Identified Western Wei Medicine Buddha on the East Wall of Mogao Cave 285 (2026)
sources.note: Original article abstract verified through publisher special-issue listing and indexed original. Direct article fetch failed. North east-wall identification is the author’s recent interpretation, not consensus or evidence of clinical care; no remedy or hospital claims.

proposedOverrides.name: Western Wei

fell.text: Yuwen Jue founded Northern Zhou in 557, ending the Western Wei dynasty.

proposedOverrides.summary: Western Wei was a short-lived northern Chinese state centered on Chang’an, remembered through government reforms and Dunhuang art.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact seams ID, historical interval 535 to 557, distinct from northern-wei, eastern-wei and northern-zhou. Single polygon explicitly coarse after Tan Qixiang, not surveyed or time-varying. Getty dates the style through 556 but expressly identifies Northern Zhou inauguration in 557; retain indexed exclusive endpoint. No aliases attached. Household miniatures and donor interpretations have explicit evidence limits; medicine is a dated 2026 hypothesis.
